implementation: ExportSelection/ExportSnapshot/captureExportSnapshot expose the agreed serializable interface; capture uses store.atomic and workspace lock, rereads workspace/revision, and reads consistent SQL metadata, inline bodies and complete audit chain. No mutation, audit append, revision bump, external blob I/O or historical replay.

Selection accepts only enabled assessable frameworks, sorts scope and record arrays, validates calendar-correct RFC3339 instants with periodStart <= asOf <= capturedAt. The review period is a label, not a coverage claim or truncation of current records.

Required dependencies field labels lineage evidence and source check/policy records outside assessed scope and records missing explicit references. Supersession closure is bounded by the evidence count cap and handles cycles.

Pre-hydration SQL aggregates reject more than20,000 workspace records across states/evidence/tasks/policies/checks/activity, more than1,000 evidence records, or more than32MiB evidence-content JSON. Counts are workspace-wide to protect current whole-workspace SQL list APIs and the complete audit chain.

All eight existing report exporters accept optional third snapshot; supplied snapshots render without live SQL reads. Scoring delegates to svc.scoreOf at one asOf, excludes future checks, applies law-effective scope, and evidence listing uses shared effectiveEvidenceState including accepted replacements.

CSV cells neutralize spreadsheet formula prefixes including leading control whitespace and preserve quote/newline escaping. Readiness, AI/CSF/SOC2 reports and OSCAL preserve explicit exclusions/reasons. Evidence CSV labels dependencies and recorded versus effective status.

SOC2 PBC emits concrete Visua-authored requests for every criterion, with identifier references rather than invented or copied AICPA wording. POAM uses author-created level-gap descriptions instead of framework requirement text.

OSCAL1.1.2 SSP and POAM use deterministic RFC4122v5 entity IDs, document IDs keyed to workspace/revision/evaluation/scope, a stable logical document ID, and explicit changing capture metadata. POAM supplies the same stable system ID as SSP.

Zero RMF level uses explained local not-implemented token; unknown categorization/user/boundary details stay explicit. No-gap POAM and no-applicable-control SSP throw useful ValidationError responses instead of invalid empty arrays or invented controls/gaps.

SSP pins official baseline/catalog URLs to immutable corpus-recorded commit and includes verified SHA256 source identities. Local tailoring actions/rationale and excluded-state reasons remain in schema-supported metadata.remarks; the source profile is explicitly OSCAL1.2.2 and is not claimed resolved or transformed to1.1.2.

limits: No full suites, PostgreSQL execution, browser server/tests, build, Docker, live database, Git operations, external provider dispatch or deployment performed by this lane.
Snapshot inline-byte preflight uses SQLite BLOB length or PostgreSQL octet_length(JSON text); only SQLite executed here. Both database variants need lead integration gates.
Full audit scope means selecting fewer frameworks does not bypass the workspace-wide safety ceilings. Large-workspace pagination/streaming is intentionally not implemented.

Schema validation does not establish operational truth, audit conclusions, or end-to-end profile resolution. SSP1.1.2 points to pinned source profile1.2.2 and explicitly disclaims a resolved tailored profile.

Report rendering uses immutable in-process registry data plus captured record arrays; no full corpus is embedded in ExportSnapshot. Bundle source metadata and immutable blob materialization remain the bundle lane responsibility.
Policies referenced by a historical evidence version may be current policy records; provenance version/hash remains intact, and bundle must describe historical bytes availability accurately.
HTTP capability/audit handling, ZIP verification, UI preview/download, full gates and deployment are owned by the parent/other workers.
